title: Congo (Democratic Republic of the) 2005 (rev. 2011)
claim: Article 69 makes the president head of state and guarantor of the constitution; Article 83 makes the president supreme commander of the armed forces; Article 85 allows proclamation of a state of urgency or state of siege after coordination with the prime minister and the chamber heads.
source_confidence_reason: Text of the constitutional framework, directly relevant to office authority and emergency powers.
ruler_attribution: Formal authority available to Tshisekedi in 2022, but not evidence of how he exercised it.
contrary_evidence: This is formal power, not proof of practical control or nuclear capability.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
claim: Freedom House says the DRC's political system is paralyzed by manipulation of the electoral process by political elites, and that opposition parties and civil society frequently criticize CENI and the Constitutional Court for lacking independence.
source_confidence_reason: Independent country report with explicit electoral-process and institutional-independence findings relevant to 2022.
ruler_attribution: Structural under Tshisekedi's administration, though not all defects are personally ordered by him.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some opposition members were released and some exiles returned under Tshisekedi.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
claim: Freedom House reports that in August 2022 opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund, formerly an ally of President Tshisekedi, was arrested for allegedly insulting the president after launching a new opposition party in July.
source_confidence_reason: Independent country report with a dated 2022 arrest tied to opposition activity.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi-era treatment of a breakaway opposition figure.
contrary_evidence: The report does not by itself prove a presidential order; it documents the arrest as a political event.

title: République démocratique du Congo 2022 - EN
claim: RSF says the national broadcaster RTNC lacks independence, local authorities commonly pressure journalists and media outlets, and the press law is obsolete and oppressive with prisons terms still attached to press offences.
locator: Media landscape, political context, and legal framework sections
source_confidence_reason: Independent press-freedom monitor with direct country-level assessment of media control and legal pressure.
period_fit: 2022 media environment and inherited legal framework
ruler_attribution: Relevant to the Tshisekedi administration's media environment and tolerance of independent information.
contrary_evidence: RSF also notes the authorities had committed to overhaul the press law, so the record includes stated reform intent.

title: World Report 2022: Democratic Republic of Congo
claim: HRW says journalists, activists, whistleblowers, and critics of government policy were intimidated, threatened, beaten, arrested, and in some cases prosecuted by authorities and security forces; it also says supporters of Tshisekedi's UDPS attacked Catholic churches and priests over an independent electoral-commission push.
locator: Freedom of Expression, Peaceful Assembly, and Media section; 2021 background retained in 2022 report
source_confidence_reason: Independent rights report tying repression and party-aligned intimidation to the ruling environment.
period_fit: Transition into 2022 and inherited political-environment baseline
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's political environment and party ecosystem, but not every incident is a direct presidential order.
contrary_evidence: The same report also notes a transitional-justice commission and limited accountability steps in 2021-2022.

title: DR Congo: Martial Law Brings Crackdown in East
claim: HRW says the military and police curtailed freedom of expression, used lethal force against peaceful demonstrations, and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and political opposition members under martial law in North Kivu and Ituri.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed independent investigation with direct attribution to the martial-law governance structure under Tshisekedi.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant because Tshisekedi's administration maintained the state of siege and set its duration.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes the government justified martial law as an anti-insecurity measure and the report is focused on abuse allegations.

title: La Feuille de route et ses préalables
claim: CENI's 2022 roadmap says its electoral work faced major politico-security, financial, legal, technical, logistical, and sanitary constraints and that the institution had weak logistical capacity.
source_confidence_reason: Primary electoral-authority statement on the practical constraints facing the 2022-2023 electoral process.
ruler_attribution: Institutional context under Tshisekedi rather than proof of his personal intent.
contrary_evidence: The same source frames these as challenges to overcome, not excuses to abandon the process.

title: Élections en RDC : Présidentielle, législatives nationales et provinciales fixées au 20 décembre 2023, voici toutes les dates
claim: The CENI set the presidential, legislative, and provincial elections for 20 December 2023, and the report says many feared a constitutional-delay 'glissement' because of the accumulated delay.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of the election calendar and the risk of constitutional delay.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's record because the 2022 calendar governed the run-up to the next contest.
contrary_evidence: Publishing a calendar is not the same as delivering a fair election or proving democratic commitment.

title: RDC: Jean Marc Kabund arrêté
claim: Actualite.cd reports that Jean-Marc Kabund was arrested on 9 August 2022, transferred to Makala prison, and that a police official said he had received an order to take Kabund there after the second audition.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local-language reporting with direct procedural details and named actors.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the Tshisekedi-era treatment of a former party insider turned opposition figure.
contrary_evidence: The article describes a judicial process and does not by itself prove presidential direction of the arrest.

title: RDC: Kabund arrêté pour 'outrage au chef de l’État, imputations dommageables et diffamation'
claim: The AFP/Actualite report says Kabund was arrested in Kinshasa and charged with outrage against the head of state, harmful imputations, and defamation after he publicly denounced Tshisekedi's camp and launched his own party.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous wire-report corroboration with the charge language and political context spelled out.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi's political-space record.
contrary_evidence: The article also records criticism that the arrest could compromise free and credible 2023 elections.

title: RDC : JED dénonce la flambée des attaques contre les médias depuis les Etats généraux de la presse
claim: JED said it had recorded 75 press-freedom violations by early May 2022, including 19 journalist arrests and 11 media closures, and that Tshisekedi had promised to accompany decriminalization of press offenses and guarantee media independence.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report quoting JED's annual observation and the president's pledge at the press conference.
ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi's media-treatment record and reform commitments.
contrary_evidence: The same item notes a presidential commitment to reform, so the evidence is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

title: DRC: One year on, 'State of Siege' used as a tool to crush dissent
claim: Amnesty said the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri was being used to crush dissent, with two activists killed by security forces and dozens of critics arbitrarily detained on trumped-up charges.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous briefing with named victims, dates, and a direct description of emergency-rule abuse.
period_fit: Within the 2022 target period; the state of siege began in 2021 but remained active throughout 2022.
ruler_attribution: Direct for the emergency regime; the abuses were carried out by security forces operating under a measure Tshisekedi kept in force and extended.
contrary_evidence: The government said the state of siege aimed to protect civilians from armed groups.
Armed-group violence also continued in the affected provinces.

title: DRC: Stop using prolonged state of siege as excuse to crush protests
claim: Amnesty said authorities threatened to crush protests in North Kivu, that critics of the state of siege had been arbitrarily detained and sometimes prosecuted by military courts, and that Tshisekedi needed to lift blanket protest bans to protect civic space.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights briefing focused on protest suppression, arrests, and civic-space restrictions.
ruler_attribution: Strong state nexus through the president-declared state of siege and the military/police authorities appointed and accountable to him.
contrary_evidence: The protests were also directed at M23 and MONUSCO, not only at the presidency.
The government framed the state of siege as a security measure.

title: RDC: Félix Tshisekedi modifie l’ordonnance sur l’état de siège et réduit les compétences pénales accordées aux juridictions militaires
claim: Tshisekedi signed an ordinance changing the state-of-siege rules so military courts handled only specified grave offenses, reducing the prior transfer of civilian criminal jurisdiction to military courts.
source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a presidential ordinance with the text and stated government rationale summarized in the article.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action, and a partial corrective response to criticism of the original emergency regime.
contrary_evidence: The underlying state of siege remained in force.
The reform did not end the broader militarization of civilian justice.

title: RDC: Félix Tshisekedi s’engage à accompagner la Dépénalisation des délits de presse et à Garantir l’indépendance des médias
claim: At the close of the media states-general, Tshisekedi said he would accompany decriminalization of press offenses and guarantee media independence, while a committee would follow up implementation.
source_confidence_reason: Direct report of the president's own statement and the reform package presented to him.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential statement, with some uncertainty because it was a commitment rather than completed reform.
contrary_evidence: The same media environment still featured arrests and pressure on journalists in 2022.
The article describes promised reforms, not yet completed changes.

title: RDC: le gouvernement adopte le texte modifiant la loi sur l’exercice de la liberté de la presse
claim: The government adopted a bill modifying the 1996 press law so it would cover freedom of information, online media, and public-service independence more explicitly.
source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous reporting of a concrete legislative reform package adopted by the cabinet.
ruler_attribution: Partial but meaningful: this was a government action under Tshisekedi's presidency, though the article does not isolate his personal initiative.
contrary_evidence: Implementation still depended on parliamentary passage and later practice.
The same period also saw continuing press arrests and pressure.

title: RDC : au regard des dérapages constatés sur les réseaux sociaux, Félix Tshisekedi demande au gouvernement de finaliser le projet du Code du Numérique
claim: Tshisekedi asked the government to finalize the Digital Code, describing the need for a repressive device adapted to cybercrime and warning media and other actors to respect the law.
source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a council-of-ministers communication and the president's framing of digital regulation.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential direction on digital controls and cybercrime regulation.
contrary_evidence: The article frames the measure as a response to cyberharassment and tribalist content, not purely political censorship.
The text reports a proposal/finalization push rather than a fully enacted law.

title: DR Congo: Provincial elections a dress rehearsal for 2023 polls
claim: Al Jazeera reported that the May 2022 gubernatorial elections were tainted by irregularities, including allegations that candidates were bribed and provincial MPs were paid to vote in ways that favored the ruling coalition.
source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with on-the-record civil-society and analyst allegations tied to a specific 2022 election process.
ruler_attribution: Partial but meaningful: the elections were run under Tshisekedi's presidency and the irregularities were attributed to the ruling coalition and its control over the process.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes some women were elected and that some seats were competitive.
It does not prove a direct presidential order for each alleged bribe.

title: RDC: Denis Kadima et le bureau de la CENI, victimes du péché originel ?
claim: A GEC/Ebuteli/BERCI survey found only 39 percent of Congolese respondents trusted the CENI to organize credible, free, and transparent elections, and the article says the lack of consensus and opacity in the CENI appointment process reinforced suspicion.
source_confidence_reason: Reports on a named survey by recognized research organizations and gives the key trust metric and explanatory interpretation.
period_fit: Directly within 2022 and focused on the pre-2023 electoral environment.
ruler_attribution: Partial: the result reflects the appointment design and operating environment Tshisekedi helped shape through CENI selection.
contrary_evidence: It is a survey of trust, not a direct finding of fraud.
The article credits Denis Kadima with technical expertise.

title: RDC-CENI : Félix Tshisekedi a investi les trois membres de l'opposition
claim: Tshisekedi formally invested the three opposition delegates to the CENI after their approval by the National Assembly, completing the commission's membership.
source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting of a dated presidential act and the composition of the electoral commission.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action that included opposition representation, though the surrounding CENI design remained contested.
contrary_evidence: Opposition parties still disputed whether the CENI was genuinely independent.
The commission's broader composition remained politically contested.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Treatment by authorities of political opponents, including those who are members of the UDPS or the FCC (2020-March 2022)
publisher: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada via ecoi.net
claim: The IRB summary says that in January 2022 FCC protests in Haut-Katanga were repressed by police, while a UDPS march the same day proceeded without police intervention, showing uneven treatment of opposition-aligned political activity.
source_confidence_reason: Government research response compiling multiple contemporaneous sources and specific 2022 incidents.
period_fit: Covers January 2022, within the target period.
ruler_attribution: Partial but meaningful: the unequal policing of opposition activity occurred under Tshisekedi's administration and reflects tolerated partisan enforcement.
contrary_evidence: The source is a research summary rather than a single primary document.
It does not prove a presidential order for the police response.

title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Treatment by authorities of political opponents, including those who are members of the UDPS or the FCC (2020-March 2022)
publisher: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada via ecoi.net
claim: The IRB summary reports that FCC lawmaker Josue Mufula was arrested and detained for criticizing the extension of the state of siege and was released the next day.
source_confidence_reason: Government research response summarizing a specific 2022 arrest with named actor and context.
ruler_attribution: Partial but meaningful: the arrest was by state authorities operating under the ruler's emergency framework, though the arresting chain is not fully spelled out.
contrary_evidence: He was released the next day, suggesting some remedial action.
The source does not establish a direct presidential order.

title: Congo names new army chief among broad military reforms
claim: Reuters reported that Tshisekedi replaced the head of the armed forces as part of military reforms and that almost the entire staff was replaced by young officers, several from the Republican Guard.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced report on concrete personnel changes and the government's own explanation of the reform.
ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment power, with some ambiguity because the government framed the change as reform for efficiency.
contrary_evidence: The government said the change aimed at boosting efficiency and military professionalism.
This is more about military control than civil political pluralism.
